NSC.note: phantompeakqualtools' normalised strand cross-correlation coefficient on each replicate's merged, filtered library, from <sample>.spp_nsc_mqc.tsv (the same value as column 9 of <sample>.spp.out). A ratio; ENCODE reads above 1.05 as enrichment. Inputs get one too: it is a library property. Verified on 2.1.0-local-narrow. A replicate sequenced over several runs is a multi-run sample and gets no backfill.

RSC.note: phantompeakqualtools' relative strand cross-correlation coefficient, from <sample>.spp_rsc_mqc.tsv (column 10 of <sample>.spp.out). A ratio; ENCODE reads above 0.8 as enrichment. Verified on 2.1.0-local-narrow; multi-run samples get no backfill.

FingerprintJSD.note: deepTools plotFingerprint's Synthetic JS Distance: the Jensen-Shannon distance between the library's fingerprint (cumulative coverage over genome bins) and a uniform, synthetic one, 0 to 1, higher meaning more enrichment. The release passes no --JSDsample, so the plain JS Distance column is never written; verified on the narrow-peak -profile test run. Read from the IP's own row of <sample>.mLb.clN.plotFingerprint.qcmetrics.txt, which also holds its control's row; inputs get none (the release fingerprints IPs only). Multi-run samples get no backfill.

DuplicationPercent.note: Picard MarkDuplicates on each replicate's merged library, before filtering. Given the config's data_format: yaml, MultiQC 1.23 writes no per-module table files: the multiqc_picard_dups rows reach only multiqc_data.json, which the harvest does not read. So the value comes from the data file of MultiQC's Picard deduplication bar plot, picard_deduplication.yaml (Picard's read counts per category, rows named <sample>_REP<n> after the config's extra_fn_clean_exts): $derived.duplication_pct is duplicate reads over duplicate plus unique reads, x100, which is Picard's PERCENT_DUPLICATION (unmapped reads left out, as Picard leaves them out). The multiqc_picard_dups tables stay first, for a MultiQC that writes them. A replicate sequenced over several runs is a multi-run sample and gets no backfill. Checked against the 2.1.0 -profile test run (fixture 2.1.0-local-test)

unmapped_files.why: FastQC reports on the raw reads; QC, not a result of the analysis.
Trim Galore logs, FastQC of the trimmed reads, and the trimmed reads themselves (with --save_trimmed): an intermediate of the registered alignment.
Library-level alignments (with --save_align_intermeds), their samtools stats, STAR logs and unmapped reads (with --save_unaligned): intermediates of the merged-library BAM the aln rule registers.
Merged, duplicate-marked and pre-orphan-removal BAMs (with --save_align_intermeds): earlier states of the filtered clN BAM the aln rule registers.
The orphan-removed alignment before sorting (with --save_align_intermeds): the same reads as the sorted clN BAM the aln rule registers.
samtools, Picard and Preseq QC of the merged alignments; summarised in the MultiQC report.
phantompeakqualtools strand cross-correlation plots and tables: QC. NSC and RSC are read from the per-sample custom-content files (sample_files) onto the D.SEQ.
deepTools plotFingerprint (IP against its control) and plotProfile QC: plotted in the MultiQC report. FingerprintJSD is read from the qcmetrics file (sample_files) onto the D.SEQ.
MACS3's peak table and gapped peaks: the same calls as the narrowPeak or broadPeak file the peaks rules register.
MACS3 summits (narrow mode): one point per registered peak, derived from the same call.

HOMER peak-to-gene annotation of the registered peaks (and of each consensus set): an annotation a user can rebuild from the registered files, and a peak row's one secondary slot is kept for its own losing variant (G-4).
MACS3 and HOMER QC plots and the FRiP, peak-count and annotation MultiQC custom-content files: QC. FRiP and the peak count are read from the per-sample files (sample_files) onto each peak row.
Each antibody's consensus peak set again as SAF and as presence/absence spreadsheets, and its UpSetR intersection files: reformats of the consensus BED the consensus rule registers.
chipseq's DESeq2 step is QC only: PCA, sample distances and the DESeqDataSet over each antibody's consensus counts, with no contrast. No differential-binding result exists to register.
IGV session file and its file list: points at the registered files, holds no data of its own.
Reference FASTA, blacklist, gene BED and aligner indexes (with --save_reference): reference files, not sample data.
